In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the holographic dual of the electric field criticality is a critical temperature, while the magnetic field criticality is the dual of the criticality of the electric field.
the Schwinger effect is the most general instability of the holographic vacuum.
the Schwinger effect is the most general criticality in the presence of an external field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the holographic dual of Schwinger criticalities is a criticality for string tension, i.e. the critical electric or magnetic field is the one that reaches the string tension of F1 and D1 strings respectively.
the criticality in the dual theory is a direct consequence of the existence of an instability in the bulk, which is the dual to the pair production process.
the criticalities in the dual field theory are related to the criticalities in bulk, i.e. the tension of the strings, and they are not modified by temperature effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, unlike ordinary QFTs, in holographic systems Schwinger criticalities are not related to a phase transition, but they are instead a purely dynamical effect.
the critical electric and magnetic field values, which are the dual to the string tension in the bulk, do not depend on the temperature.
the presence of a large t’ Hooft coupling in the bulk, which is a generic feature of strongly coupled gauge theories, is crucial for the existence of the Schwinger criticalities.
